items.title: Satire, parody exception to copyright law could allow more exploiting of local artists’ work, MPs told
items.summary:
The Copyright (Parody and Satire) Amendment Bill was pulled from the biscuit tin in November 2024. Sponsored by Green MP Kahurangi Carter, it would create a carve-out in the country’s copyright laws that would mean anyone engaging in parody and satire is able to engage in “fair use” of copyrighted material. [...] Carter said while her bill did not deal with AI, any work using copyrighted material, whether AI or otherwise, would still have to comply with New Zealand’s Fair Dealing laws, which define specific purposes - research and study, criticism and review and news reporting, for example - under which protected work can be used without permission.

But Browning said the relationship between copyright and AI was unresolved.

“This matters for the bill before you today. [...] AD

Political cartoon by Sharon Murdoch - members of NZ’s creative industry have told a select committee that a proposed carve-out of copyright law that would mean parody or satire work can be used under ‘fair use’ provisions.Sharon Murdoch

A select committee has been warned today that a satire and parody exception to copyright laws, if approved, could more easily allow AI companies to exploit NZ creatives’ work.
